column3: “harlot” renders “prostitute.”
NASB supplies “When it was told” (as in the Greek) and “Let us wait”; the Hebrew begins “To the Gazites, saying.”
“bars” is plural for the Hebrew singular “bar.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“lords” renders “rulers” (also in verses 8, 18, 23, 27, 30); “eleven hundred pieces of silver” renders “one thousand and one hundred silver.”
“afflict” renders “humble.”
“any other man” renders “one of humankind.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“she had men lying in wait” renders “the ambusher was sitting for her”; “touches” renders “smells.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“tightly” renders the doubled verb; “which have not been used” renders “with which no work has been done.”
NASB supplies “For”; “the men were lying in wait” renders “the ambusher was sitting.”
NASB adds in braces “and fasten it with a pin … like any other man,” words found in the Greek but not in the Hebrew.
NASB continues the braced addition from verse 13 to “wove them into the web”; the Hebrew reads only “and she fastened it with the pin.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“his soul was annoyed to death” renders “his soul was short to die.”
“all that was in his heart” renders “all his heart.”
“once more” renders “this time”; “money” renders “silver.”
“had him shave off” renders “she shaved off”; “afflict” renders “humble.”
“as at other times” renders “as time upon time.”
“a grinder in the prison” renders “grinding in the house of the prisoners.”
“after” renders “as.”
“hands” renders the Hebrew singular “hand.”
“hands” renders the Hebrew singular “hand”; “Who has slain many of us” renders “who has multiplied our slain.”
“in high spirits” renders “their heart was good”; “amuse” and “entertained” render the same verb.
NASB omits “Let me go” (literally “let me rest”) before “Let me feel.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Lord GOD” renders “Lord Yahweh”; “at once … for my two eyes” renders “one vengeance for my two eyes.”
“braced himself” renders “supported himself.”
“Let me die” renders “Let my soul die”; “bent” renders “stretched out.”
